title: Meeting a New Colleague
context: Hai người gặp nhau trong ngày đầu tiên ở văn phòng.

transcript.speaker: Nam
transcript.text: Hello. I'm Nam. What's your name?

transcript.speaker: Mai
transcript.text: Hi, Nam. My name is Mai. I'm new here.

transcript.speaker: Nam
transcript.text: Nice to meet you, Mai. What's your job?

transcript.speaker: Mai
transcript.text: I'm a tester. And you?

transcript.speaker: Nam
transcript.text: I'm a developer. Our desks are near the window.

questions.question: What is Mai's job?
questions.explanation_vi: Mai nói: 'I'm a tester'.

questions.question: Where are their desks?
questions.explanation_vi: Nam nói: 'Our desks are near the window'.

title: A Simple Interview Question
context: Người phỏng vấn hỏi ứng viên những câu đơn giản về kỹ năng.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Good morning. Do you use a computer every day?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I use it at home and at work.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Can you write Python?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: No, I can't. But I can write HTML.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Good. Do you like working in a team?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Yes. I like my team very much.

questions.question: What can the candidate write?
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'I can write HTML'.

questions.question: Where does the candidate use a computer?
options: B) At home and at work
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'I use it at home and at work'.

title: The Computer Is Slow
context: Một nhân viên gọi cho bộ phận hỗ trợ vì máy tính chậm.

transcript.speaker: Staff
transcript.text: Hello. My computer is very slow.

transcript.speaker: Support
transcript.text: Is the internet slow too?

transcript.speaker: Staff
transcript.text: No, the internet is good.

transcript.speaker: Support
transcript.text: OK. Please close all the windows and start the computer again.

transcript.speaker: Staff
transcript.text: Thank you. Now it is fast.

questions.question: What is the problem?
questions.explanation_vi: Nhân viên nói: 'My computer is very slow'.

questions.question: What does the support person say to do?
options: C) Close the windows and start the computer again
questions.explanation_vi: Bộ phận hỗ trợ nói: 'close all the windows and start the computer again'.

title: Talking About Your Last Job
context: Hai đồng nghiệp trò chuyện về công việc trước đây trong giờ nghỉ.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Where did you work before you came here?

transcript.speaker: Duc
transcript.text: I worked at a small game company in Hanoi for two years.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Did you like it?

transcript.speaker: Duc
transcript.text: Yes, the people were friendly, but the salary wasn't very good.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Is this job better?

transcript.speaker: Duc
transcript.text: Yes, it is. The work is harder, but I'm learning more.

questions.question: How long did Duc work at the game company?
questions.explanation_vi: Duc nói: 'for two years'.

questions.question: What was the problem with Duc's old job?
options: B) The salary wasn't very good
C) The office was too far
D) The work was too hard
questions.explanation_vi: Duc nói: 'the salary wasn't very good'.

title: Scheduling an Online Interview
context: Nhân viên nhân sự gọi điện để hẹn lịch phỏng vấn trực tuyến.

transcript.speaker: Recruiter
transcript.text: Hello, is that Thu? I'm calling about your application.

transcript.speaker: Thu
transcript.text: Yes, this is Thu. Thank you for calling.

transcript.speaker: Recruiter
transcript.text: Can you do an online interview on Thursday at ten?

transcript.speaker: Thu
transcript.text: Sorry, I'm busy on Thursday morning. Is the afternoon possible?

transcript.speaker: Recruiter
transcript.text: Yes. How about two o'clock?

transcript.speaker: Thu
transcript.text: That's perfect.

transcript.speaker: Recruiter
transcript.text: Great. I'm going to send you the link by email.

questions.question: When is the interview?
questions.explanation_vi: Hai bên thống nhất vào chiều thứ Năm, lúc hai giờ.

questions.question: How will Thu get the link?
questions.explanation_vi: Nhà tuyển dụng nói: 'send you the link by email'.

title: Daily Stand-up Meeting
context: Nhóm phát triển báo cáo nhanh công việc trong cuộc họp buổi sáng.

transcript.speaker: Manager
transcript.text: Good morning. Quang, what are you doing today?

transcript.speaker: Quang
transcript.text: Yesterday I finished the search page. Today I'm working on the login page.

transcript.speaker: Manager
transcript.text: Any problems?

transcript.speaker: Quang
transcript.text: Yes, I can't download the new photos. I need a password.

transcript.speaker: Manager
transcript.text: OK, I'm going to send it to you after this meeting.

questions.question: What did Quang finish yesterday?
questions.explanation_vi: Quang nói: 'Yesterday I finished the search page'.

questions.question: What does Quang need?
questions.explanation_vi: Quang nói: 'I need a password'.

title: Walk Me Through Your CV
context: Ứng viên trình bày ngắn gọn học vấn và kinh nghiệm làm việc.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Could you tell me a bit about yourself?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Of course. I studied computer science in Can Tho and graduated in 2021.

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Since then, I've worked as a mobile developer at a travel company.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What are you responsible for there?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I'm responsible for the Android app, and I also help to test new features.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: And why do you want to leave?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I enjoy my job, but I'd like to work on a larger product with a bigger team.

questions.question: What is the candidate responsible for?
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'I'm responsible for the Android app'.

questions.question: Why does the candidate want to leave?
options: A) To work on a larger product with a bigger team
B) To earn a higher salary
C) Because the job is boring
D) To move to another city
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên muốn làm 'a larger product with a bigger team'.

title: Describing a Difficult Bug
context: Ứng viên kể về một lỗi khó mà họ đã tìm ra và sửa.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Can you tell me about a difficult bug you fixed?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Yes. Last year, our app crashed for some users, but only on older phones.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: How did you find the cause?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I borrowed an old phone and read the error logs. The app was using too much memory because the photos were too large.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: So what did you do?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I made the photos smaller before loading them. After that, the crashes stopped.

questions.question: Which users had the problem?
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'only on older phones'.

questions.question: What caused the crashes?
options: D) Too much memory used because of large photos
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng dụng dùng quá nhiều bộ nhớ vì ảnh quá lớn.

title: Explaining a Deployment Process
context: Một kỹ sư giải thích quy trình phát hành cho nhân viên mới.

transcript.speaker: New Hire
transcript.text: How is the code released to customers?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: First, you open a pull request. Then the tests are run automatically.

transcript.speaker: New Hire
transcript.text: What happens if a test fails?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: If a test fails, you can't merge your code. You have to fix it first.

transcript.speaker: New Hire
transcript.text: And after the merge?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: The code is deployed to a test server. If everything is fine, we release it on Tuesday.

questions.question: What happens if a test fails?
options: A) The code cannot be merged
B) The code is released anyway
questions.explanation_vi: Kỹ sư nói: 'If a test fails, you can't merge your code'.

questions.question: When is the code released?
questions.explanation_vi: Kỹ sư nói: 'we release it on Tuesday'.

title: Self-Introduction in a Technical Interview
context: Ứng viên đang giới thiệu về kinh nghiệm backend và cloud infrastructure.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Could you walk me through your background and your recent experience?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Sure. I have over three years of experience as a backend developer, focusing on high-availability PostgreSQL clusters.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What have you been working on recently?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: For the past eight months, I've been moving our services from virtual machines to Kubernetes on AWS.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What has been the biggest benefit so far?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Our deployment time has dropped from about an hour to under ten minutes, which means we can release much more often.

questions.question: How many years of experience does the candidate have as a backend developer?
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói rõ: 'I have over three years of experience as a backend developer'.

questions.question: What has been the main benefit of the move?
questions.explanation_vi: Thời gian triển khai giảm từ khoảng một giờ xuống dưới mười phút.

title: SQL or NoSQL?
context: Người phỏng vấn hỏi ứng viên cách chọn cơ sở dữ liệu cho một ứng dụng đặt vé.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Which database would you choose for a ticket booking system?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I'd go with a relational database, mainly because we need transactions to stop two people from booking the same seat.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: But what if traffic grew tenfold?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: If that happened, I'd first add read replicas and a cache for browsing events, since most traffic is read-only.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ever use NoSQL here?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Possibly for storing user activity, although I'd keep the bookings themselves in the relational store.

questions.question: Why does the candidate prefer a relational database?
options: A) It is free to use
B) Transactions prevent double booking of seats
C) It is easier to learn
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói cần transaction để ngăn hai người đặt cùng một ghế.

questions.question: What would the candidate do first if traffic grew tenfold?
options: A) Add read replicas and a cache
B) Move all data to NoSQL
C) Buy a larger single server
D) Limit the number of users
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'I'd first add read replicas and a cache'.

title: Handling Disagreement in a Code Review
context: Ứng viên trả lời câu hỏi hành vi về bất đồng với đồng nghiệp.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague.

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: A senior engineer wanted to add a new library for a feature I thought we could build in a few lines.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: How did you handle it?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Rather than arguing in the comments, I suggested a quick call and we compared both options.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What was the outcome?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Despite my initial view, I realised the library handled several edge cases I'd missed, so we kept it.

questions.question: What did the candidate suggest instead of arguing in comments?
options: A) Asking the manager to decide
C) A quick call to compare the options
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'I suggested a quick call and we compared both options'.

questions.question: What was the final decision?
options: A) They built the feature without the library
C) They replaced the senior engineer's code
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'so we kept it'.

title: Presenting Yourself for a Lead Role
context: Ứng viên vị trí trưởng nhóm kỹ thuật trình bày hành trình nghề nghiệp.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What makes you the right person to lead this team?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: What I'd highlight is the transition I led at my current company, where we went from one fragile release a month to deploying several times a day.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What was your specific role in that?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I wrote the original proposal and secured buy-in from leadership, but the part I'm proudest of is having coached two engineers who now own the platform.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: So you've stepped back from it?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Deliberately, yes. I see my job as making myself redundant in any given area.

questions.question: What is the candidate proudest of?
options: A) Coaching two engineers who now own the platform
C) Reducing the size of the team
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói phần tự hào nhất là đã kèm cặp hai kỹ sư hiện làm chủ nền tảng.

questions.question: What does the candidate mean by 'making myself redundant'?
options: A) Planning to leave the company soon
B) Building teams that no longer depend on them in that area
questions.explanation_vi: Ý là bồi dưỡng người khác để nhóm không còn phụ thuộc vào cá nhân họ ở mảng đó.

title: Designing a URL Shortener
context: Buổi phỏng vấn system design về dịch vụ rút gọn liên kết.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: Let's design a URL shortener. Where would you begin?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I'd start by clarifying the read-to-write ratio. Assuming it's heavily skewed towards reads, say a hundred to one, the design should be optimised around redirects.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: How would you generate the short codes?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Hashing the URL invites collisions, so I'd favour a pre-allocated counter range per application server, encoded in base 62.

transcript.speaker: Interviewer
transcript.text: What happens if a server dies with part of its range unused?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Those codes are simply lost. Given a keyspace in the trillions, that's a trade-off I'd happily accept in exchange for avoiding coordination on every write.

questions.question: Why does the candidate avoid hashing the URL?
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói: 'Hashing the URL invites collisions'.

questions.question: What does the candidate accept as a trade-off?
options: A) Slower redirects for most users
D) Losing some unused codes when a server dies
questions.explanation_vi: Mã chưa dùng bị mất, đổi lại không cần phối hợp trên mỗi thao tác ghi.

title: Reviewing an Incident
context: Nhóm kỹ thuật họp phân tích sau một sự cố kéo dài.

transcript.speaker: Facilitator
transcript.text: Let's establish the timeline. When did we first become aware of the issue?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: Customers reported errors at 14:05, whereas our alerts didn't fire until 14:22.

transcript.speaker: Facilitator
transcript.text: Why the seventeen-minute gap?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: The alert was tied to average latency, which masked a failure affecting only one region.

transcript.speaker: Facilitator
transcript.text: And had it been per region?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: We would have been paged within two minutes. It's the aggregation, rather than the threshold, that needs changing.

questions.question: What was the gap between customer reports and the alert?
questions.explanation_vi: Khách báo lỗi lúc 14:05, cảnh báo kích hoạt lúc 14:22, chênh lệch mười bảy phút.

questions.question: What does the engineer believe needs changing?
options: B) The way metrics are aggregated
D) The region hosting the service
questions.explanation_vi: Kỹ sư nói: 'It's the aggregation, rather than the threshold, that needs changing'.

title: The Staff Engineer's Pitch
context: Cuộc trò chuyện giữa giám đốc kỹ thuật và ứng viên cấp staff về phạm vi ảnh hưởng.

transcript.speaker: Director
transcript.text: Your CV is remarkably light on the usual trophies. Why is that?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Much as I could list launches, the work I'd stand behind is largely invisible: the outages that never happened and the projects I talked us out of.

transcript.speaker: Director
transcript.text: That's a difficult thing to verify.

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: Admittedly. Which is why I'd point you to the decision records. Three years on, the reasoning has either held up or it hasn't, and I've annotated where mine didn't.

transcript.speaker: Director
transcript.text: You kept a record of your own errors?

transcript.speaker: Candidate
transcript.text: I'd contend that's the only part of the archive worth reading.

questions.question: How does the candidate propose to substantiate their claims?
options: A) By providing references from former managers
D) By pointing to annotated decision records
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên đề nghị xem 'the decision records', có ghi chú những chỗ họ đã sai.

questions.question: What does the candidate imply about the record of their errors?
options: A) It is the most valuable part of the archive
B) It should be kept confidential
C) It was a requirement of the company
D) It contains very few entries
questions.explanation_vi: Ứng viên nói đó là 'the only part of the archive worth reading'.

title: Debating Consistency Guarantees
context: Hai kỹ sư tranh luận về mức nhất quán cho một hệ thống tồn kho đa vùng.

transcript.speaker: Engineer A
transcript.text: I'd insist that inventory counts be linearizable. Anything less and we oversell.

transcript.speaker: Engineer B
transcript.text: Only if you model stock as a single number. Partition it into per-region allocations and each region can decrement independently, without a cross-region round trip.

transcript.speaker: Engineer A
transcript.text: Until one region exhausts its share while another sits on a surplus.

transcript.speaker: Engineer B
transcript.text: Granted, in which case it requests a transfer, and only that rare path need pay for coordination.

transcript.speaker: Engineer A
transcript.text: So you'd confine consensus to the exceptional case.

transcript.speaker: Engineer B
transcript.text: Precisely. Should a transfer stall, we'd reject the sale, which the business has told us it prefers to overselling.

questions.question: How does Engineer B avoid a cross-region round trip on every sale?
options: A) By using a stronger consensus protocol
C) By partitioning stock into per-region allocations
D) By moving all inventory to one region
questions.explanation_vi: Kỹ sư B đề xuất 'per-region allocations' để mỗi vùng tự trừ độc lập.

questions.question: What happens if a transfer between regions stalls?
options: A) The sale proceeds and is reconciled later
D) Stock is borrowed from a supplier
questions.explanation_vi: Kỹ sư B nói: 'Should a transfer stall, we'd reject the sale'.

title: Is Kubernetes Justified Here?
context: Một buổi đánh giá kiến trúc phản biện đề xuất áp dụng Kubernetes cho một đội nhỏ.

transcript.speaker: Reviewer
transcript.text: You're proposing Kubernetes for four services and a team of five. Forgive me, but the case strikes me as tenuous.

transcript.speaker: Architect
transcript.text: The current scripts have become untenable. Each deployment hinges on tacit knowledge held by one person.

transcript.speaker: Reviewer
transcript.text: That argues for better automation, not necessarily for an orchestrator whose operational overhead may well exceed the problem it solves.

transcript.speaker: Architect
transcript.text: Were we self-hosting, I'd concede the point. A managed control plane obviates most of that burden.

transcript.speaker: Reviewer
transcript.text: Most, perhaps. Upgrades, networking and security policy remain yours, however.

transcript.speaker: Architect
transcript.text: Fair. Let's trial a managed container service first and revisit this only if we outgrow it.

questions.question: What problem with the current scripts does the architect identify?
options: B) They are written in an old language
C) They cost too much to host
D) Deployment relies on one person's tacit knowledge
questions.explanation_vi: Kiến trúc sư nói mỗi lần triển khai phụ thuộc vào 'tacit knowledge held by one person'.

questions.question: What do they finally agree to do?
options: A) Trial a managed container service first
C) Keep the current scripts unchanged
D) Hire a dedicated operations team
questions.explanation_vi: Kiến trúc sư đề xuất 'trial a managed container service first'.
